study type: Prospective long-term follow-up study (including elements of a randomized controlled trial and a cohort study)
exposure: Hysteroscopic removal (morcellation or cold loop resection)
cohort: The study cohort comprised 261 women who had undergone removal of retained products of conception (1-4 cm) by either hysteroscopy or ultrasound-guided electric vacuum aspiration and desired future conception.
finding: Hysteroscopic removal and ultrasound-guided electric vacuum aspiration for retained products of conception showed no significantly different effects on subsequent live birth rate, pregnancy rate, time to conception, or overall pregnancy complications, although both groups experienced a high risk of placental complications.
